rows.title: Inflation

rows.figure: Control of the strait now formally disputed
rows.read: Saturday night formalized the dispute: the IRGC declared Hormuz 'closed' and claimed 5+ more tanker attacks in 24h — CENTCOM chief Cooper fired back that the strait is 'controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran' and 'remains open for business' (400 ships, ~100M barrels transited). The NY Post counts 12 vessels attacked in the week ended Friday — the largest weekly UKMTO tally since the war began, with a new RPG-from-small-boat attack type. The IRGC's two-tanker mine claim has a second wire (AFP) but still zero independent confirmation. Sunday is the signing test.

rows.read: Friday's closes stand: Nov WTI $101.41 (first settle over $100 since Sep 21), Dec Brent $109.86 — the ~$8.5 Brent-WTI spread is still a wide geopolitical premium (normal ~$3-5). Overnight, Ukrainian drones hit the Petersburg Oil Terminal — Russia's largest Baltic export terminal (damage unconfirmed) — a fresh physical supply-risk headline that collides with the Graham waiver's deflation (no Oct-18 duty bite; 60-day review). Saturday's Hormuz ledger: record attack week, IRGC mine claim unverified, Cooper's rebuttal. Sunday's oil open ~5pm CT prices both forces.
